sources.citation: Anon. (18th c.). 'Doctrina para los viejos chonos' (catechism; published in Bausani 1975), es.wikisource transcription
sources.note: The sole primary text (c. 40 short lines); no accent marks on Chono words (the only accented forms are Spanish: Espíritu, zelà); no basis for a stress statement.

sources.citation: Ibar Bruce, Jorge. 1960. 'Ensayo sobre los indios Chonos e interpretación de sus toponimias.' Anales de la Universidad de Chile 117: 61-70
sources.note: Only a syllable note on toponyms (p. 67-68): 'Las voces chonas son por lo general monosilábicas y se combinan de a dos, tres y hasta cuatro para formar un nombre geográfico. Terminan generalmente en consonante'; 'las voces chonas tomaron con el tiempo un acento español' refers to Hispanicised pronunciation, not a stress rule.

sources.citation: Cárdenas A., Renato; Dante Montiel Vera & Catherine Grace Hall. 1991. Los chono y los veliche de Chiloé. Santiago: Ediciones Olimpho. 277 pp. Chapter I 'El idioma de los chono o waiteka', pp. 139-152.
sources.note: The language chapter argues Chono was distinct from Veliche (Mapudungun), from Tehuelche/Chon and from northern Kawesqar, recounts the Tentori/Bausani catechism find, and compiles a Spanish-Chono lexicon, untranslated catechism words, numerals, 'partículas gramaticales' from the Doctrina (ko/kon masculine, se/sen feminine, -tau locative/1sg/past, qui 'ergativo') and toponymic elements (-ac, -ach, -ao, -ec, -lin, -tau). sources.citation: Viegas Barros, J. Pedro. 1990. 'Dialectología qawasqar.' Amerindia 15
sources.note: Mentions Chono/'wayteka' only to reject Llaras Samitier's 1967 wordlist and to review the classification debate; nothing on Chono stress.

sources.citation: Urbina Burgos, Rodolfo. 1988. 'Los chonos en Chiloé: itinerario y aculturación.' Chiloé: Revista de divulgación del Centro Chilote 9: 29-42 (Memoria Chilena digitisation MC0012568, dated 2002 in the record).
sources.note: no phonology content — only that 'la lengua chona fue cayendo en desuso' under Chilote acculturation.

sources.citation: Hanisch Espíndola, Walter. 1972. Itinerario y pensamiento de los jesuitas expulsos de Chile (1767-1815). Santiago: Editorial Andrés Bello. 332 pp. Section 'Lenguas y pueblos de indios', pp. 236-239, printing the 'Noticia de la lengua de los indios chonos' and the 'Catecismo de los viejos chonos' from the ms. 'Breve relación de los indios de Chile' (Biblioteca Nazionale V.E., Roma, Mss. Ges. 1407).
sources.note: Prints the 'Noticia' ('Estos indios tienen su lengua particular muy diferente de la lengua general de Chile y Chiloé..') and the full question-answer catechism (Luentaumet Dios? / Jo padre.. Sua ta vla) 'sin traducción', followed by notes on Caucahue ('es muy gutural') and Calen/Taijataf numerals. The Chono words carry no accent marks except one printed 'quénau' and the diaeresis in 'üeñec'/'eüjuhau'; Hanisch adds no linguistic commentary. Nothing on stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Llarás Samitier, Manuel. 1967. 'El grupo chono o wayteka y los demás pueblos Fuegopatagonia.' Runa: Archivo para las Ciencias del Hombre 10(1-2): 123-194. Buenos Aires: Universidad de Buenos Aires, Instituto de Ciencias Antropológicas. (sec. VII 'El lenguaje' pp. 162-165; 'Vocabulario wayteca (Chonos del golfo de Peñas)' pp. 184-187).
sources.note: Sec. VII is ethnohistorical (Ferrufino's 1612 remark that the 'lengua chona.. es muy diferente y más dificultosa en la pronunciación que esta general', mutual (un)intelligibility reports). The vocabulary marks an acute accent on many items (mókstap 'cabeza', tékfo 'brujo', kénkapon 'arco iris', wékorq 'blanco', pénkel 'frío'..), mostly on the first syllable, but the only analytic remarks are 'Las terminaciones ko, kon, konk, son masculinas y se, sen son femeninas' and 'La mayor parte de sus vocablos se forman mediante la composición de voces elementales' (p. 187). sources.note: No phonology content and none possible per the author: LANGUAGE (p. 48): 'Not a single word of the Chonoan language has come down to us, except, perhaps, the word Chono itself, three names of unidentified birds (colman.., optem, piupigue..) and a few tribal, personal, and geographical names.. sources.citation: Cooper, John M. 1917. Analytical and critical bibliography of the tribes of Tierra del Fuego and adjacent territory. BAE Bulletin 63
sources.note: Records that the only Chono linguistic material then known was Fitz-Roy's three-word 'Chono' vocabulary; discusses whether Chono was a distinct stock or an Alacaluf dialect; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: [Anon.] 1916. 'Anthropology at the Washington Meeting.' Science n.s. 43 (1120): 865-866 (16 June 1916) - printed abstract of John M. Cooper, 'Fuegian and Chonoan Tribal Relations' (the ICA 19 paper later printed as Cooper 1917: 445-453, A's work 5).
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. The abstract's whole linguistic content: 'A comparison of fifteen available vocabularies and some additional stray words shows with fair clearness that the Alacalufan tongue is spoken by all the non-Yahgan canoe-using Indians.. as far as Port Grappler or Messier Channel. The Chonos, now perhaps extinct, spoke a non-Araucanian and non-Tehuelchean language, but whether it was a distinct stock or an Alacalufan dialect is uncertain.'

sources.note: No remark on Chono pronunciation or accent; the only 'acent-' string is 'la densidad se acentuaba' (population). Toponym lists and oral traditions of Chono-Chilote raids only.
